question: What do we call nutrients that our bodies cannot make on their own, so we must get them from our food?
explanation: Spot on! Essential nutrients are the ones your body can't manufacture by itself, so eating them is a must for survival.

question: Why is checking 'nutrient density' often better than just counting calories when looking at a patient's diet?

options.A: It measures the amount of vitamins and minerals relative to the calories
options.B: It calculates the exact percentage of body fat a food item will produce
options.C: It determines how fast the digestive system will break down a meal
options.D: It shows the total monetary cost of the food items consumed

explanation: You got it! Nutrient density tells you how many good vitamins and minerals you get per calorie, helping avoid empty calories.

question: Which type of food nutrient gives us the highest amount of energy (calories) per gram?
explanation: Correct! Fats pack about nine calories per gram, which is more than double what carbs or proteins give us.

question: A patient is healing from major surgery and needs help repairing tissue and fighting infection. Which nutrient should you focus on?
explanation: Well done! Proteins break down into amino acids, which are the building blocks your body uses to heal wounds and build immunity.

question: Which group of vitamins is more likely to build up in the body and cause toxicity if taken in excess for a long time?
explanation: Exactly! Fat-soluble vitamins get stored in the liver and fatty tissues instead of being peed out, so too much can cause a buildup.

question: What is the main job of minerals like sodium and potassium in our bodies?

options.A: Storing excess kilocalories for times of fasting
options.B: Regulating fluid balance and nerve transmission
options.C: Acting as primary structural units for muscle fibers
options.D: Providing the main source of daily cellular energy

explanation: Spot on! Sodium and potassium are key electrolytes that keep our fluids balanced and help nerves send signals to muscles.

question: Which hormone tells the kidneys to hold onto water when the body is getting dehydrated?
explanation: You got it! Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) tells your renal tubes to reabsorb water so you don't lose too much in your urine.

question: Why do we count water as a nutrient even though it gives us zero calories?

options.A: It breaks down into simple sugars inside the stomach lining
options.B: It is essential for life, acting as a medium for all metabolic reactions
options.C: It stimulates the production of digestive enzymes in the pancreas
options.D: It converts directly into structural tissue during growth phases

explanation: Correct! A nutrient is anything needed for survival and body chemistry—it doesn't have to provide energy to be vital.

question: Which type of dietary fiber is best known for adding bulk to stool and keeping things moving smoothly in the gut?
explanation: Spot on! Insoluble fiber doesn't break down easily, so it adds bulk and helps prevent constipation.

question: A patient is taking extra fiber for constipation. What important advice must you give them?

options.A: Increase fluid intake significantly alongside the extra fiber
options.B: Take the fiber supplement immediately before going to bed
options.C: Cook all high-fiber vegetables until they are completely soft
options.D: Eliminate all fats from the diet to make the fiber work faster

explanation: Well done! Fiber acts like a sponge—if patients don't drink enough water with it, it can actually make constipation worse or cause a blockage.

question: What is the main protective job of antioxidants found in fruits and vegetables?

options.A: Neutralizing unstable free radicals that damage cells
options.B: Acting as direct hormones to lower blood pressure
options.C: Speeding up the mechanical digestion of dietary fats
options.D: Providing the main structural foundation for muscle tissue

explanation: Correct! Antioxidants fight off unstable free radicals so they don't damage our cells and DNA.

question: Why are phytochemicals from plants not officially classed as 'essential nutrients' even though they are great for our health?

options.A: They are entirely artificial compounds created during food processing
options.B: The body does not suffer an immediate deficiency syndrome if they are absent
options.C: They only exist in animal tissues rather than plant-based foods
options.D: They provide too many calories for daily metabolic requirements

explanation: Spot on! Missing essential nutrients causes specific deficiency diseases, whereas missing phytochemicals just means you miss out on extra health boosts.

question: Which deficiency disease is caused by a serious lack of Vitamin C?
explanation: You got it! Without enough Vitamin C, your body can't make collagen properly, leading to scurvy (bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds).

question: Which of these is NOT a reliable way for a nurse to assess a patient's overall nutritional status on its own?

options.A: Observing clinical signs such as skin condition and muscle wasting
options.B: Performing anthropometric measurements like height and weight
options.C: Asking the patient what they ate yesterday without any other data
options.D: Reviewing biochemical laboratory values such as serum albumin

explanation: Spot on! A single 24-hour food recall can easily be inaccurate and doesn't give the full clinical picture without physical checks and lab results.
